title: WF03 Stage11 cycle3: integration harness reset used all-or-nothing truncate; verification blocked by concurrent integration runners/cache lock contention
description: Cycle3 diagnosis identified that tests/integration/helpers.zig resetTestData used one multi-table TRUNCATE guarded by a blanket ServerError catch, so one missing table could skip cleanup for all transient tables and produce cross-test contamination. The fix changed resetTestData to per-table best-effort truncation. During verification, overlapping integration runners in this session caused .zig-cache AccessDenied and unstable aggregate evidence collection.
root_cause: Test harness cleanup implementation was brittle (single TRUNCATE statement), and verification execution was affected by concurrent zig build test-integration processes sharing the same cache/database.
error_detail: error: failed to rename compilation results ... AccessDenied (when overlapping integration runs held .zig-cache artifacts)
resolution: Updated resetTestData to truncate transient tables individually via truncateTableBestEffort so missing legacy tables no longer disable all cleanup. Build validated (zig build exit 0). Aggregate integration verification remains pending clean rerun without concurrent runners.
verification: Batch re-triage 2026-08-10 (WF03-batch-GH280-301-triage-20260810): source-read confirms tests/integration/helpers.zig:628,631,692 implements per-table best-effort truncateTableBestEffort exactly as described in resolution, with an explicit GH-402 doc comment. Closing on source evidence per issue's own resolution note.
prevention: For integration harness cleanup, avoid multi-table statements that fail atomically in heterogeneous schemas; use per-table best-effort cleanup and enforce single active aggregate runner per workspace.
